Subject: Adaptive measurement window & rollback playbook — hosted API SLO request

Hi Samir,

Thanks again for the call yesterday — appreciate the candid signal about your tranche-based traffic patterns during end-of-month billing. As discussed, attached is a short proposal for an "adaptive measurement window" approach to our hosted API p50/p95 commitments. The goal is to give Capitol Health stronger guardrails (clear rollback triggers, audit logs, and mitigation steps) while avoiding overly conservative static windows that inflate cost or block rollouts.

High-level summary (attachment: adaptive-window-draft.pdf):
- Target commitments: p50 = 30ms, p95 = 220ms (region: us-east) measured with a dynamic epoch.
- Measurement model: sliding 24h epoch with a burst-aware sub-sampling layer for ephemeral spikes; we would run a shadow evaluation for 7 days before an amendment takes effect.
- Canary & rollback playbook: automatic 10% canary for 48 hours; if p95 rises > 30% vs baseline for two consecutive 1h buckets, autoscale + priority routing engaged; if not recovered within 3 hours, automatic rollback to previous model variant.
- Audit & evidence: 30-day immutable latency traces, per-request route tags, and SOC2-aligned export for audits.

Ask: Please confirm whether this structure addresses Capitol Health's procurement risk appetite and whether you want us to insert these mechanics into an amendment (DocuSign link draft provided). If you prefer different numeric targets or a longer shadow period, flag which pieces you want changed and we'll update.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm acceptance-in-principle of the adaptive-window logic.
2) Redwood runs a 7-day shadow test (no SLA enforcement) on your production traffic shape.
3) If results look good, legal issues a narrow amendment with the canary & rollback appendix.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call this week to walk the tech bits.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai

Tessa — thanks for the write-up and attachments. A few quick things from our side:

- We like the canary + automatic rollback idea, but need a clear definition of "baseline" for the percent change trigger. Is baseline a rolling 7d median, or will Redwood define a static pre-amendment baseline?
- For audits: Procurement will require a canned export format (CSV + JSON trace) and an export cadence. Can you confirm retention window and whether exports can be pushed to our S3?
- SOC2: we'll need evidence that the shadow runs are isolated and that any cached data isn't leaked into production variants. Please include the isolation controls in the amendment.

Finally, our security team is sensitive to automated rollback impacting availability if the system oscillates during a data migration. We need an explicit dampening rule (e.g., minimum 1h between rollbacks during scheduled maintenance).

Can procurement and security review the updated doc this week? If so we'll aim to sign an amendment next week conditioned on the shadow test results.

—Samir
Director, Platform Reliability
Capitol Health

Samir, Tessa — quick technical clarifications and implementation notes from infra:

1) Baseline definition: we recommend a rolling 7d median (per-region, per-route) as baseline. That gives resilience to gradual shifts and aligns with our telemetry retention. We'll also keep a "pre-amendment snapshot" baseline for audit/comparison.

2) Measurement windows & sampling: primary measurement = sliding 24h epoch with 5m buckets for alerting and hourly aggregation for SLO claims. For burst suppression we use a probe-based sub-sample that excludes traffic tagged as known scheduled bursts (customer-provided calendar) and weights background traffic. This reduces false positives during predictable maintenance.

3) Canary/rollback logic: suggested algorithm (we put a copy in canary-rollback-thresholds.xlsx):
   - Start: 10% canary for 48h with elevated tracing.
   - Alert condition: p95 > baseline * 1.30 for two consecutive 1h aggregations.
   - Recovery actions: immediate priority routing to warm nodes + autoscale; if p95 remains > baseline * 1.20 after 3 hours, execute rollback.
   - Dampening: no automatic rollback during user-scheduled maintenance windows; minimum 1h cooldown between rollbacks. Manual override always available to Capitol Health.

4) Exports & retention: we can deliver a daily CSV export and a weekly JSON trace bundle to your S3 (bucket policy-based delivery). Traces for 30 days retention are standard; longer retention can be added as an opt-in. All exports include per-request route tags and model-variant ids.

5) Isolation for shadow runs: our private shadow lanes are logically isolated from production variant state; KV cache and model weights are segregated. We'll include a SOC2-mapped control matrix in the amendment.

If you want, I can run a short internal sim (12h synthetic spike) to validate the dampening logic before we start the 7d shadow.

—Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

- Apr 28: Deliver shadow report + CSV/JSON export for first 7 days.
- Apr 30: Procurement & Security review amendment; legal prepares DocuSign appendix if approved.
- May 3: Canary rollout (10% traffic) begins; 48h canary window.

Key commitments from Redwood:
- Baseline = rolling 7d median + immutable pre-amendment snapshot.
- Canary rollback criteria as described by Karthik; minimum 1h cooldown between auto-rollbacks and no auto-rollback during scheduled maintenance windows.
- Audit export delivered to your S3, 30-day retention by default.
- SOC2 control matrix included in amendment.

If that looks good, I'll instruct Legal to draft the narrow amendment (DocuSign: AMENDMENT-78921). If Procurement wants a longer shadow period or stricter thresholds (e.g., p95 tolerance of 1.10 instead of 1.20 recovery), call it out and we will scope the cost impact.

Thanks — I'll plan a 30-minute sync with Procurement on Apr 19 to walk the MAP unless you prefer a different cadence.

Best,
Tessa
